neighbours.label: the word that completes a long clausal subject ('the way in which X works is ___'), a clause boundary after the predicate
fire: The way in which this printer cuts glass is remarkable. It leaves no marks at all.
The manner in which these birds build nests is extraordinary. They weave grass into tubes.
The process by which the cheese is aged is unusual. It sits in a cave for a year.
The way that the old clock keeps time is curious. It relies on a falling weight.
The method with which they dye the wool is impressive. It uses only local plants.
The speed at which this vine grows is astonishing. It covers a wall within weeks.
The way in which the film handles grief is surprising. Nobody ever cries on screen.
The route by which the river reaches the sea is strange. It flows underground for miles.
quiet: This remarkable printer cuts glass with a laser. It leaves no marks at all.
These extraordinary birds build nests from grass. They weave it into tubes.
This unusual cheese is aged for a year. It sits in a cave near town.
This curious old clock keeps time well. It relies on a falling weight.
These impressive dyers colour the wool by hand. It takes only local plants.
This astonishing vine grows along the wall. It covers the stones within weeks.
This surprising film handles grief with care. Nobody ever cries on screen.
This strange river reaches the sea near town. It flows underground for miles.
